A fresh look at the manifold

A compact pool for reviewing spectral history and deciding what Palomar can newly test.

Current working selection

Either candidate manifold region · historical r ≤ 18.5 · at least 60 continuous minutes with airmass ≤ 1.5 and Moon separation ≥ 60°.

The same constraints must hold throughout each qualifying window.

This replaces the earlier candidate selection. The old Moon distances were incorrect. These are review candidates; final science weights, exposure times, and an observing sequence are pending. Expanded W1 coverage is still being processed.

Click a candidate to inspect it. Shaded cells mark the two existing regions; neither region predicts the current spectral state.

The allocated nights

All times are Palomar local time (PDT), including October. Counts overlap between nights. The Moon is above the horizon throughout these windows.

How to use this review

First compare W1 behavior with the dates and broad-line states of earlier spectra. Then ask what a new spectrum could establish: a first transition, persistence, recurrence, or a test of an uncertain prediction. No on/off forecast or discovery probability has been assigned.

Brightness is historical. Moon separation and airmass are geometric cuts, not a guarantee of line S/N. Exposures need current brightness and line-specific sensitivity estimates.

The manifold uses normalized W1 light-curve shapes; its axes are not a clock. The two regions have different selection and validation histories.
